CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Fetal tissue (uncultured solid tissue)
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Analysis of fetal tissue

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) - Subtelomere screening
2. Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) - Aneuploidy screening

METHODOLOGY
MLPA Analysis:
- SALSA MLPA P036 and P070 Human Telomere kits used for comprehensive subtelomeric region analysis
- Covers all chromosome subtelomere regions (1p-22p, 1q-22q, Xp/q, Yp/q)
- DNA extracted from uncultured solid tissue
- Fragment analysis performed on ABI 3730 Genetic Analyzer
- Data analyzed using Coffalyser.Net software

QF-PCR Analysis:
- Multiplex QF-PCR for rapid aneuploidy detection
- Chromosomes analyzed: 13, 18, 21, X and Y
- STR markers used:
  - Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S634, D13S742
  - Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390
  - Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1446
  - X chromosome: AMELX, DXS6803, DXS6809
  - Y chromosome: AMELY, SRY
- Analysis performed on uncultured tissue DNA

RESULTS

MLPA SUBTELOMERE ANALYSIS
Result: No abnormality detected
- All subtelomeric regions show normal copy number (ratio 0.85-1.15)
- No deletions or duplications identified
- Quality metrics within acceptable range

QF-PCR ANEUPLOIDY SCREENING
Result: No abnormality detected
- Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern
- Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern
- Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern
- Sex chromosomes: Female pattern (XX)
  - AMELX: Single peak consistent with two X chromosomes
  - No Y chromosome markers detected
- No evidence of triploidy

INTERPRETATION
The combined MLPA and QF-PCR analyses show:
- No imbalance found in tested regions
- Results consistent with female sex chromosome complement (46,XX)
- No evidence of triploidy, aneuploidy or subtelomere imbalance
- Normal female genetic complement detected

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
1. Maternal cell contamination: While no evidence of maternal contamination was detected, low-level contamination cannot be completely excluded
2. Mosaicism: Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected with these methods
3. Small segment imbalance: Deletions or duplications smaller than the probe coverage regions will not be detected
4. Balanced rearrangements: These techniques do not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
5. Detection sensitivity: QF-PCR is limited to chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y; other aneuploidies would not be detected

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Scientist
